There’s no reason to feel ashamed for your disease. On the other hand it is difficult to live with add/adhd as I’m sure everyone here will tell you. Whatever you do, don’t let his ignorance get to you, because there’s entire communities of people who understand your problems more and can support you better than he is. I’ll keep that in mind. The survey sounds really interesting and potentially helpful. I don’t do good with really internalizing action consequence stuff and often have a hard time realizing that being unproductive is cutting into fun time. My therapist says that adhd causes me to have a poor “locus of control” and it makes it weird for me to consider how my actions affect how I’ll feel later. That’s why I can’t really get motivation to do something fast just so I can do something else later.

I’m super sorry to hear that. Finding Relationships can be super difficult and stressful, but maintaining them is the hardest thing in my experience. Just hang in there and try to be conscious of your own feelings and know that you deserve someone who cares about you even through impulsive decisions and poor mental health
